p: The garden has two main entrances: the East Gate on Inverleith Row and the West Gate on Arboretum Place, where you'll also find the John Hope Gateway visitor centre. Pick whichever suits your route, but a loop that takes you in one gate and out of the other covers most of the highlights.

Look out for the Chinese Hillside, planted with species from China, complete with a pavilion and waterfall, and the Queen Mother's Memorial Garden, a peaceful spot with a shell-lined pavilion. The rock garden is a joy in spring, when alpine plants burst into colour.

Seasons bring their own magic. Spring is all about rhododendrons and blossom, summer brings long evenings and bursts of colour, and autumn sets the trees on fire. In winter, the Christmas at the Botanics light trail is hugely popular, so book early.

Love it here? RBGE has three other gardens across Scotland: Benmore near Dunoon, Dawyck near Peebles and Logan near Stranraer, each with its own character. They're well worth a detour if you're travelling around the country.

One last thing: the squirrels here are bold little beggars. Keep an eye on your sandwiches, and on the kids' crisps, because they've clearly done this before. It's all part of the charm of a few easy hours in one of Edinburgh's calmest corners.
